title: One TOI-682 timing fit keeps its periapses aligned while all five 7:3 angles circulate for 1,000 Newtonian years
abstract: We test five published coplanar TOI-682 timing fits near the 7:3 period ratio. In the 1,000-year Newtonian test of the 8.12-Earth-mass fit with a mean outer period of 16.00232 days, all five planar critical angles make about 444 turns. The periapse direction difference stays between -21.41 and +13.38 degrees. This fit has apsidal alignment without 7:3 mean motion trapping in the tested interval. A 0.645-Earth-mass fit has only 0.042 net turns in one angle, but a range of 1.023 turns; we do not label it secure libration. The past timing losses differ by only 1.12. We preserve the source states, numerical tracks, checks and code. These are point-fit tests, not observations of resonance, posterior odds or evidence for a migration path. Newtonian forces, fixed source parameters, five selected states and finite duration limit the result. No new telescope data are used.

display.caption: One published timing state has apsidal alignment with circulating 7:3 angles. Another has slow net winding in one angle. These are finite Newtonian tests of point fits.
